method: Two independent reviewer agents with no shared context: one compared lm.rs, rtl.rs, recognition.rs, geometry.rs, assembly.rs, order.rs and runtime.rs function by function against indra-ocr 1.1.2 (pipeline.py, lm.py, rtl.py, rec_preproc.py, line_mask.py, order_post.py, vocab.py, math.py) and executed the reference on the port's own fixtures; the other audited the owner's code rules (no dyn/Vec/clone/to_owned/anyhow, bounded arrays, error handling), allocation behaviour on the request path, the Python arm's metering, and test adequacy. Every finding was verified against the code and either fixed in the commit named or recorded with a reason. Both reviewers independently found the list-marker defect (P1/R1).

reviews.scope: port versus the Python reference, function by function

findings.rust: assembly.rs:Page::tidy (BULLETS const line 29; `BULLETS.contains(marker)` in the marker loop) and the unit test tidy_joins_markers_to_their_item_by_page_direction
findings.claim: The reference's BULLETS is a *set of single characters* and `t in BULLETS` is set membership; the port's BULLETS is a &str and `BULLETS.contains(marker)` is a substring test. The two disagree for the empty string and for any multi-character contiguous slice of the bullet string.
findings.effect: Every line whose decoded text is empty or whitespace-only (every reading under MIN_CONF keeps its box with text ""; checkboxes, rules, specks and empty form fields produce these on ordinary pages) is treated by the port as a list marker. If another non-empty line overlaps it vertically by half a height and starts within -0.3..2.5 heights after it (before it on an RTL page), the port drops the empty line, prefixes the neighbour's text with a space (`"" + " " + item`), and widens the neighbour's box to the union, which also changes its reading-order features. The reference keeps the empty line as its own empty output line and leaves the neighbour untouched. Page.text therefore differs (one fewer "\n", a leading space, possibly a different line order). Multi-character bullet strings such as "●○" or "∙*" are likewise markers only in the port. The 1.1.2 source is unambiguous; the port's comment and test encode the wrong rule.
findings.resolution: 5a9a415 fix(engine): list markers are single bullet characters; reviewer findings

findings.rust: assembly.rs:Page::assemble (`let h = (f64::from(b[3]) - f64::from(b[1])).max(1.0)`) and assembly.rs:gutter (h parameter)
findings.claim: The reference computes the line height for the gap split and the gutter test as a float32 subtraction of two float32 box coordinates (then converts to float); the port subtracts in f64, which is exact. The values differ by up to one float32 ulp when the box's top and bottom have different float32 exponents (boxes near the top of the page, or very tall boxes).
findings.effect: Only when a token gap lies within ~1e-6 line heights of exactly 3.0 h (split), 1.6 h / 0.5 h / 0.35 h (gutter) can the split decision differ, and the tightened segment boxes may differ in their last float32 bit. No change on real pages except at exact ties.
findings.resolution: 5a9a415 fix(engine): list markers are single bullet characters; reviewer findings

findings.python: order_post.py:order_top_down (line 117) as reached from order_xycut/xycut_blocks after a cut
findings.rust: order.rs:top_down (sort key `.then(a.cmp(&b))`) as reached from order.rs:xycut
findings.claim: Inside a sub-range produced by an XY cut, the reference's fallback `order_top_down` uses Python's stable `sorted` over the sub-range's *current* order (the parent's argsort by the cut axis), so lines with an equal (row, x0) key are ordered by the parent's lo coordinate; the port breaks the same tie by the original global line index. This is distinct from the accepted NumPy-argsort tie rule: when the parent's lo values are distinct, the reference order is well defined.
findings.effect: Two lines in the same row band with identical x0 (near-duplicate or stacked detections) under a horizontal-cut parent may swap positions. At the root block (ids ascending) and for grid blocks (members ascending) the two rules coincide.
findings.resolution: 5a9a415 fix(engine): list markers are single bullet characters; reviewer findings

findings.python: math.py:MathReader.read (early stop `np.mean(probs[b]) < MATH_MIN_CONF - EARLY_STOP_MARGIN`; acceptance `float(np.mean(probs[k]))` vs MATH_MIN_CONF in pipeline.recognize)
findings.rust: math.rs:mean and its two uses in Reader::read (`mean(&self.probabilities[row][..n + 1]) < 0.8`, `confidence < 0.9`)
findings.claim: The reference's mean of the per-token probabilities is NumPy's float64 pairwise (8-accumulator) sum; the port sums sequentially in f64. For eight or more tokens the two roundings can differ in the last bit.
findings.effect: A math line whose running mean sits within ~1e-16 of 0.8 (early stop) or 0.9 (replace the line) can be stopped/accepted differently, changing that line's text. Practically only at exact boundaries; math is off by default.
findings.resolution: 5a9a415 fix(engine): list markers are single bullet characters; reviewer findings

findings.python: order_post.py:line_features (np.log on float32), det_post.py:decode (np.exp float32), math.py:MathReader.read (np.exp float32 softmax), order_post.py:decode_blocks_order (`G @ a @ G.T` via BLAS dgemm)
findings.rust: order.rs:features (`.ln()` on f32), geometry.rs:decode_detector (`(-logit).exp()`), math.rs:top_probability (`.exp()`), order.rs:decode_with_scratch (sequential f64 loops for the block means)
findings.claim: Transcendental functions and the block-mean matrix product are evaluated by different libraries (NumPy's SIMD float32 log/exp and BLAS vs Rust's libm and explicit loops). The port documents this and the recorded parity run shows up to ~1.7e-5 in order logits. I could not confirm on this host whether the deployment NumPy's float32 log/exp are correctly rounded, so the magnitude is uncertain; the algorithms are otherwise identical (same operand order for the sigmoid/log-sigmoid, same pairwise sum emulation in sum32).
findings.effect: Feature values and logits can differ by an ulp; reading order or a detector pixel at the 0.5 boundary can flip only at near-ties. No systematic difference.
findings.resolution: Transcendental and BLAS rounding differ by design between arms; the frozen protocol's 1e-5 tolerances and exact integer checks cover it, as in the 2026-10-18 comparison.

findings.claim: The reference's BULLETS is a Python set, not a str: pipeline.py:918 `BULLETS = set("•◦▪▫●○■□‣⁃∙*")`, tested at :959 `t in BULLETS or ENUMERATOR.fullmatch(t)` — exact single-character membership. `"" in set(...)` is False in Python, so an empty line is never a marker and stays as its own (empty) output line; the Rust `str::contains` makes every whitespace-only line a marker (`"...".contains("")` is true) and joins it to the nearest non-empty line on the same row within 2.5 heights, dropping the line and prefixing the item with a space. It also accepts adjacent-pair substrings such as "•◦" or "∙*" that Python rejects. Empty lines are common (every reading under MIN_CONF keeps its box with empty text, pipeline.py:512-516). The unit test `tidy_joins_markers_to_their_item_by_page_direction` (assembly.rs:504-520, expecting "\n after blank") and the assertion `BULLETS.contains("")` at :461 enshrine the divergence. Measured on the committed reference records (tests/evidence/2026-10-21-parity-1-1/reference-macos-arm64/*/details.json, applying the Rust rule to the reference's final boxes/texts): 3 of 19 pages change — jingbao-1930-500 (20 empty lines joined), lectaurep-riant-01 (3), sankaracarya1925-03-body (1). Those are precisely the corpus pages the frozen 1.1.2 run skipped, so the pending native parity gate would not catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: Match on exactly one character: `let mut it = marker.chars(); let bullet = matches!((it.next(), it.next()), (Some(c), None) if BULLETS.contains(c));` and use `bullet || enumerator(marker)`. Update the test so the empty line is kept and "after blank" is unchanged, and replace the `BULLETS.contains("")` assertion with `!bullet("") && !bullet("•◦")`. Correct the doc comment (set membership, not substring).
findings.resolution: 5a9a415 fix(engine): list markers are single bullet characters; reviewer findings

findings.claim: `finish_characters` (every CJK/RTL/world line and every math line) and `page_direction` (every CJK line) run on the request path through icu_normalizer 2.3.0's `Decomposition`, whose buffer is `SmallVec<[CharacterAndClass; 17]>` (icu_normalizer-2.3.0/src/lib.rs:546). SmallVec spills to the heap once more than 17 pending non-starters accumulate before the next starter, so a line with 18 or more consecutive combining marks allocates (and frees) on the Rust heap. The group vocabularies contain 103 (RTL), 208 (world) and 6 (CJK) Mn/Me tokens, so a noisy CTC reading can produce such a run. This replaced unicode-normalization's `TinyVec<[_; 4]>` (spill after 4), so ad3411d is an improvement, but the owner's documented exception (`unicode_normalization::nfc()` inline SmallVec) no longer describes the code and the new comment's 'never allocates for ordinary text' is conditional, not a bound. The allocations gate (tests/allocations.rs) never exercises NFC at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Either bound the input (reject or truncate a run of more than 17 combining marks before normalising, returning `EngineError::Limit`), or document the data-dependent allocation explicitly in docs/native-engine.md and the comment, and add an allocation-gate case that normalises a 17-mark run (zero churn) so the threshold is pinned.
findings.resolution: 5a9a415 fix(engine): list markers are single bullet characters; reviewer findings (seventeen-mark run in the allocation gate; the limit is stated in assembly.rs and docs/native-engine.md; a line needs eighteen consecutive combining marks to spill)

findings.claim: No test calls `decode_ctc` with `lm: Some(..)`. findings.claim: For a version-2/3 `.npy` member of 10 or 11 bytes the indices `bytes[10]`/`bytes[11]` are out of bounds and panic instead of returning `EngineError::Shape`. Startup-only and unreachable in production because `indra_models::verify` hash-checks the archives first, but it is an unguarded fixed index and `malformed_archives_are_rejected` does not cover the v2 header.

findings.claim: lm.py:206 keeps a candidate with `v >= log_floor`, which drops NaN; the port's `value < log_floor` keeps NaN. `Output::extract` validates all six recogniser shapes but not the finiteness of `blank`/`topv` (only `confidences` are range-checked in `decode_ctc`:725-731, and `classify` checks its probabilities), so a non-finite top-k value would propagate into the beam scores rather than being rejected or ignored as in the reference.
findings.suggested_fix: Write the test as the reference does (`!(value >= log_floor)`), or reject non-finite `blank`/`topv` in `Output::extract` next to the shape checks.

findings.claim: The stated bound is wrong in both directions: the longest base token in the locked meta.json vocabulary is 15 bytes (`\longrightarrow`, `\leftrightarrow`, `\Leftrightarrow`), math tokens are up to 20 bytes, and base tokens never enter `collapsed`/`normalized` at all (`decode_tokens` writes base text straight into `self.text`). The real consumers are group characters (≤ 512 × 3 bytes) and math text (≤ 319 × 20 bytes ≈ 6.4 KB), so the 64 KiB capacity is sufficient; the documentation that is supposed to prove it does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate the comment with the actual consumers and bounds (group chars ≤ 1,536 B before NFC; math ≤ 319 tokens × 20 B) and add a `const _: () = assert!(...)` on `3 * MAX_TOKENS` and `20 * 319` against `LINE_SCRATCH_BYTES`.
findings.resolution: 5a9a415 fix(engine): list markers are single bullet characters; reviewer findings (comment restated; const assertions on the scratch bound)

findings.claim: The reference's `split_line` and `gutter_cuts` compute `h = max(1.0, float(box[3] - box[1]))` (pipeline.py:570, :608) with the subtraction in float32 before widening; the port subtracts in f64, which differs in the last bits whenever the f32 difference needs rounding, so a `3h`/`1.6h`/`0.35h` comparison exactly at a boundary can flip. `decode_ctc` (recognition.rs:716) correctly mirrors `recognize` (pipeline.py:479-481), which converts to float before subtracting.
findings.suggested_fix: In `assemble` and `gutter` use `f64::from(b[3] - b[1]).max(1.0)` so the subtraction rounds in f32 as the reference does.
findings.resolution: 5a9a415 fix(engine): list markers are single bullet characters; reviewer findings

beam_search floor pruning with a full beam (8 beams): an extension that cannot reach the floor is never scored; compare against an exhaustive 2-3 step enumeration.
Routing boundary: a class probability exactly equal to `route_sure` is not sure (strict `>`); `route` with count 0; `prepare` rejecting MAX_LINES+1 boxes.

tidy after fixing R1: empty line kept and never a marker; '•◦' is not a marker; chained joins (marker -> item that is itself later a target); overlap exactly 0.5·min(h); gap exactly -0.3·h and exactly 2.5·max(h); `wide` exactly 3h; narrow '--' (two dashes) kept.

page_direction has no unit test: tie (rtl == ltr -> false), CJK jamo composed before counting (one syllable = one letter), math text counted, `count == 0` lines ignored, base `\alpha` letters counted as LTR.

assemble splitting: a 3h token gap cut with tight boxes (0.35h), a gutter cut needing three other edges, a whitespace-only part dropped, `parts == 1` text left untrimmed, a group-script line flipped per part on an RTL page.
Page::write: order length mismatch and out-of-range index return `Shape`; multi-frame separator.
xycut_blocks: gap exactly equal to the median height cuts (`>=`), `gap_y == gap_x` prefers the horizontal cut, a single line, and a block whose inner order is then decided by `xycut`.
is_dark_line: boundary `hi - med == 2·(med - lo) + 8` is false; a box partly outside the page; a 1-pixel box (n = 1, so `min(i+1, n-1)` = 0); a box with b[0] > b[2] after truncation.

geometry: `unrotate_box` with a non-zero angle against reference values (only the identity is tested); `fill_batch` with `window = 3` and `dark = true` checking 96 rows and inverted ink; `reserve_window` growth preserving the arena contents; `crop_geometry` pixel-limit rejection.

rtl: a neutral cluster adjacent to an LTR run on an RTL base (e.g. 'אב abc, גד'), a leading combining mark with no base, `rtl_base` tie (equal counts -> false), `base_rtl = Some(false)` on an RTL-majority line.
lm.rs `npy`: a version-2 header shorter than 12 bytes returns `Shape` rather than panicking (R4); `bits.npy` absent -> DEFAULT_BITS; `order * bits > 61` rejected; unsorted/duplicate keys rejected.
Allocation gates for `Page::assemble`/`tidy`/`finish_characters` (including a 17-mark run) and `request_allocations` on the committed synthetic RTL/world/vertical fixtures (R8).

continuous: a vertical frame enters `Phase::Base` with no flagged rows and proceeds through World/Rtl to Cjk; tall-window arena growth in `invoke`; `route_line` on a shared Script batch increments `dual_read_lines` per owner.

Native parity: the three corpus pages where the empty-line join changes text (jingbao-1930-500, lectaurep-riant-01, sankaracarya1925-03-body) are exactly the skipped cases; either run them in the hosted gate or add a unit case with empty lines beside text.
reviews.missing_tests_disposition: The decode_ctc language-model boundaries, the bullet rule, the pairwise mean, the v2 npy header and the normaliser gate were added in the fix commit; the remaining cases are recorded here as follow-ups for the layer's next fix commits.
confirmed_ok: Rule 1: no `dyn`, no `anyhow` anywhere in indra-engine/src; `thiserror` in lib.rs; no `unwrap`/`expect` outside `#[cfg(test)]` in any in-scope file (grep of lm, rtl, recognition, geometry, assembly, order, runtime, math, continuous, batching, lib). `const fn` used for Params consts, Script accessors, Routing::new, Line::empty, rtl::Scratch::new, Pool::new, mirror, extend_hash, rotation_code, vertical_box_back, Phase::{group,route,shared,model,next}, Model::{bits,order,max_logp,admits}, ModelSettings::fetch_options.

clippy (`DOCS_RS=1 cargo clippy -p indra-engine --all-features --lib --tests --examples --benches -- -D warnings`) reports nothing except the known macOS-only `rustix::fs::mkfifoat` failure in tests/perf_control.rs.

Rule 2 beam search: `Scratch::new()` (lm.rs:380-391) is the only allocation and is documented startup; `beam_search` uses only the boxed pools and three small stack arrays (candidates 8, extensions 64, order 72); `Model::load` is documented startup-only and all `format!`/`collect` calls are inside it.

Rule 2 strings: `recognition::append` caps every String at MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES (recognition.rs:799-809); `Page.text` has 2×MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES and marker joins are guarded at :285-287; `Lines.math_text` has MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES; `collapsed`/`normalized` (64 KiB) only ever hold group characters (single-char tokens, ≤ 3 bytes each, verified from meta.json: 0 multi-character tokens in vocab_cjk/rtl/world) or math text (≤ 319 tokens × ≤ 20 bytes); the server's output buffer is `String::with_capacity(MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES)` (indra-server/src/service/state.rs:59). None can reallocate.

Rule 2 arenas: tall-window growth is explicit and logged in both `reserve_window` (recognition.rs:253-268) and continuous `invoke`; the crop arena grows only at a high-water mark (geometry.rs:222-229); `Mat::from_slice` in `line_input` borrows the crop (opencv 0.101 BoxedRef) and the remaining `Mat::default()`/`core::rotate`/`warp_affine` outputs in `upright` are OpenCV native allocations covered by the exception.

Rule 2 stack: largest per-request arrays are `features` (64 KiB), `probabilities` (16 KiB), `mirrored`/`boxes` (16 KiB) plus ~150 KiB transient in `order::decode_with_scratch`/`xycut_blocks`; the LM pools (≈164 KiB), bidi scratch and `math::Reader` tables (240 KiB) are boxed or engine-owned; far below the 8 MiB worker stack.

Rule 3 beam search: CANDIDATES = BEAM·(TOP_K+1) = 72 holds 8 own entries + 64 extensions; `extensions` = BEAM·TOP_K; `candidates` ≤ TOP_K (loop bound); `len == MAX_TOKENS` is checked before `tokens[slot][len]` (lm.rs:544); `t as u16` and `(len+1) as u16` are bounded by the `timesteps > MAX_TOKENS` rejection (lm.rs:428-435); `history << bits` and `1 << bits·(order-1)` cannot overflow because load rejects `order·bits > 61` and `bits == 0`.

Rule 3 rtl: MAX_CLUSTERS = 513 is checked before every cluster write (rtl.rs:160-162); units ≤ clusters; `last` is only read after `start` was set; multi-character tokens never reach `flip` (group vocabularies are single characters and the math vocabulary contains no R/AL characters).

Rule 3 routing/recognition: `Routing::prepare` rejects > MAX_LINES; `route` requires `probabilities.len() == count·4`; `probabilities[..boxes.len()·4]` is cut from `[f32; MAX_LINES·4]`; `Output::extract` validates ids/conf/lengths/blank/topv/topi shapes (incl. `[rows, T, 8]`) and `T ≤ MAX_TOKENS` before any slicing; `length()` bounds `n ≤ T`; `decode_ctc` validates `index < MAX_LINES`, ids ≥ 0 and ≤ vocab, probabilities in [0,1].
Rule 3 order: `xycut`/`xycut_blocks` work stacks hold disjoint sub-ranges, so ≤ n ≤ MAX_LINES entries; `best_cut` is only called with len > 1; `median` only on non-empty slices.

Rule 3 geometry: `is_dark_line` truncates like Python `int()`, returns false for empty/outside boxes, `n ≥ 1` guarantees `n - 1` is safe, histogram/cumulative indices are 0..=255; `crop_geometry` validates finiteness and ordering and caps pixels; `decode_detector` validates plane size and label map bounds.

Rule 4 deadlines: per line in `assemble`, per marker in `tidy`, per angle in `estimate_skew`, per 65,536 labels in `decode_detector`, per batch and per crop in `fill_batch`/`text`/`classify`, per step in the math decoder, per cluster/sweep in `order`; `beam_search` is bounded at 512 steps × 72 candidates per line and runs inside the per-batch checks.

Semantics: `Model::logp` reproduces `logp_keys` (history_seen[0] forced true after the lookup so hb[0] applies; `longest` = leading seen prefix; suffix cumsum from the longest level down; uniform floor `-ln V`); `bound()` reproduces `max_logp`.

Semantics: `beam_search` reproduces lm.py 163-254 — blank-skip (`b0 > log_skip`), candidate floor (modulo NaN, R5), own-entry repeat collapse, floor only with a full beam, `reach` pruning with the 1e-9 slack, merge into an existing prefix keeping its score, stable descending sort (insertion order on ties), first maximum; the parity test checks 15 recorded pipeline calls bit-exactly on the locked archives.

Semantics: `rtl::flip` reproduces rtl.py (clusters on Mn/Me, kinds R/AL vs L/EN/AN, `_runs` stop/end handling, LTR runs kept whole and other clusters mirrored and reversed on an RTL base, RTL runs reversed in place on an LTR base, mirror map); `rtl_base` counts only bidi class L against R/AL; `page_direction` counts L* letters over raw tokens, composing NFC only for CJK, which is the only vocabulary containing U+1100 (Vocab.jamo).

Semantics: dual read strictly-higher rule (`conf <= line.best` -> keep old) matches pipeline.py:509; LM gate `MIN_CONF <= conf < gate` matches :487; beam inputs are `[:n]` slices as in :491-493; conf stays the greedy mean after rescoring; positions `ix0 + (step + 0.5)·stride·f` match :501; read order Base, World, Rtl, Cjk matches meta.json key order (vocab, vocab_world, vocab_rtl, vocab_cjk) and the group sets are disjoint so order only affects stats; `Params::GROUP` (0.2, 1.5, 0.95) equals meta.json lm_params for cjk and world; the RTL recogniser has no `lm_rtl.npz` in the lock.

Semantics: `tidy` leader rule (`≥3`, wide `w ≥ 3h` in f32, lone dash kept), marker overlap/gap rule, strict `<` best gap, box union, heights not recomputed after a join, and `enumerator` (`\d{1,3}` via the Nd table, ASCII letter, 1-5 roman) all match pipeline.py:928-992 except R1; `python_whitespace` matches `str.strip()`/`split()`.

Semantics: `is_dark_line` percentiles reproduce `rec_preproc._percentiles` (searchsorted side='right', NumPy lerp from the nearer end, `hi - med > 2(med - lo) + 8`); `crop_geometry` reproduces `crop_line` for window 1 and 3; `xycut_blocks` reproduces `order_post.xycut_blocks` (median height min_gap, `gy >= gx`, upper/left first, `order_xycut` inside blocks); `upright` reproduces `__call__`/`_turn` (skew on the preview, orientation on the straightened preview, quarter turn, second skew estimate on the turned preview for classes 1/3/VERTICAL).

Rule 6 (backend/server.py:151-167): after wrapping, `engine.rec` is the SessionMeter, so `src = tall if sess is self.rec else crops` (pipeline.py:465) still selects the tall window because `groups` is built from `self.rec` (pipeline.py:440, :452); `engine.lms` is re-keyed by `id(metered)` for rec, cjk and world and `engine.lm` refreshed; group sessions are re-keyed too; `get_outputs()` is only read in `__init__` before wrapping; `get_providers()` and the lms/script-group checks run before wrapping; `MathReader` only calls `.run` on `cls`/`enc`; `document.py:62` touches vocabularies only. Nothing else in indra_ocr 1.1.2 depends on session identity or on methods SessionMeter lacks. `ConfiguredOCR.recognize` matches the 1.1.2 signature `(gray, boxes, batch=64, vertical=False)`.
configuration.rs: `engine.lm` and `engine.route_sure` are plumbed through CLI, file, `EngineSettings` and `validate_runtime` (0.5..=1.0, finite) consistently with `EngineConfig::validate`.

scripts/generate-indra-tables.py derives BIDI_RTL/BIDI_L/BIDI_LTR/MARK/LETTER/EAST_ASIAN_WIDE/UPPER/DECIMAL from CPython 3.13 unicodedata with the same predicates rtl.py/pipeline.py/order_post.py use, and TEXT_STARTS_LETTER from `category(token[0]).startswith('L')` matching `nxt[:1].isalpha()`.
